mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below a 12-month moving average triggers a negative demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 6% and FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% AND FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and high interest rate regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, coupled with a flat or declining GDPC1, indicates a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND GDPC1 flat or declining for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both GDPC1 and HOUST above their respective 3-month moving averages signals a synchronized expansion in aggregate demand and housing activity, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 3-month MA AND HOUST > 3-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
